## Polymorphism with `Shape`

Most of pgl is static: the pair of [shapes](shapes.md) is known at compile time and the tightest result type is chosen there. [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") is the runtime alternative — a `std::variant` over every shape, with the whole common interface forwarded to whichever one it holds.

```C++
pgl::Shape p = pgl::Point(3,7);
pgl::Shape s = pgl::Segment(1,4,2,9);
pgl::Shape r = pgl::Rectangle(1,4,2,9);
if (r.contains(p))
    std::cout << r << " contains " << p << std::endl;
if (r.intersects(s))
    std::cout << r << " intersects " << s << std::endl;
```

The alternatives, in storage order, are [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."), [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices."), [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect."), [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."). A default-constructed [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") holds the [`EmptyShape`](shapes.md#emptyshape).

Like every other shape, [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") is templated on a point type, `pgl::Shape<pgl::Point<int>>` by default. All alternatives share that same point type: a `Shape<Point<int>>` can hold a `Segment<Point<int>>` but not a `Segment<Point<double>>`. The [exact type aliases](types.md#exact-type-aliases) name the common instantiations, `pgl::EShape` for `pgl::Shape<pgl::EPoint>`.

```C++
pgl::Shape<pgl::Point<double>> e;   // holds EmptyShape
e.empty();                          // true
e = pgl::Disk<pgl::Point<double>>(...);
e.empty();                          // false
```

[`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") does what the shape it holds does, and throws `pgl::unsupported_operation` (a `std::logic_error`) when that shape cannot: a bounding box of a [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), the vertices of a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), the [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5d1599cde109c2e6d956ce7cc18b5700 "Returns the connected pieces of the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") of a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") and a [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."). The message names the operation and the alternatives, e.g. `pgl::Shape: bbox(Line) is not supported` or `pgl::Shape: intersection(Segment, Disk) is not supported`. Nothing answers in place of a missing implementation, and no pair is listed anywhere: a pair gains [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") support as soon as the concrete member for it exists.

### Storage against geometry

Two vocabularies never share a word. `is…`, `getIf…` and `as…` are geometric and answer as the stored shape does; `holds…`, `getIfHolds…` and `asHeld…` ask which alternative is stored.

```C++
pgl::Shape c = pgl::Triangle(2,2,2,2,2,2);  // collapsed to a point
c.holdsTriangle();                          // true: the Triangle alternative is stored
c.holdsPoint();                             // false
c.isPoint();                                // true: the point set is a single point
c.getIfPoint();                             // std::optional holding (2,2)
c.getIfHoldsTriangle()->isPoint();          // the same answer, through the stored triangle
```

- `s.holds<T>()`, `s.getIfHolds<T>()`, `s.asHeld<T>()`: Whether the stored alternative is `T`, a pointer to it (`nullptr` otherwise), and a reference to it (throws `std::bad_variant_access` otherwise). Every alternative, [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane.") included, has named shorthands: [`holdsSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a2bddac495410d46d919e57f7232caa7d "Tests whether the stored alternative is Segment."), [`getIfHoldsSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a923436c6454d2780020546eca6ccb6d1 "Returns a pointer to the stored Segment, or nullptr when another alternative is stored."), [`asHeldSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a4bd35187cb6d81327b4fa11d0bd7a1ae "Returns the stored Segment; throws std::bad_variant_access when another alternative is stored."), and so on.
- [`s.visit(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a8986f1fa84abb169306763c85268365c "Calls f with the stored alternative."): Calls `f` with the stored alternative, in a `const` and a mutable overload. [`s.variant()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a1c23beb343593491d4de84eed560bed4 "Returns the underlying variant, for code that needs it as a variant.") exposes the `std::variant` itself, for `std::visit` over several shapes at once.

### Construction and conversion

- A [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") is constructed and assigned from any alternative implicitly.
- It is also constructible from a `std::variant` of alternatives, or a `std::optional` of one — the return types of the typed [intersection](shape_methods.md#intersection) methods. An absent optional gives the empty shape, and deduction reads the point type off the variant, so `pgl::Shape i = a.intersection(b);` names the right type for a result that is not a range.
- [`pgl::pieces(result)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/namespacepgl.html#adcfea9cef0756ab14b871f0431eb1d1c "Splits the result of a concrete operation into its connected pieces, each wrapped in a Shape.") splits any concrete result into a `std::vector<Shape>`, one per connected piece, dropping what covers no point. It accepts a shape, an optional, a variant, a vector of either, a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") (one piece per component) and a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.").

```C++
auto i = pgl::Shape(a.intersection(b));   // point, segment or empty
auto p = pgl::pieces(a.intersection(b));  // the same, as pieces
```

- `pgl::Shape<pgl::Point<double>>(s)` converts a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") over another point type alternative by alternative, and converts a concrete shape of another point or label type into the alternative of its kind. Both conversions are explicit; the conversion between [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") types throws for an alternative with no such conversion.
- Naming the alternative's type extracts it — `pgl::Segment<> q(s)`, or a `static_cast` — throwing `std::bad_variant_access` on a mismatch, as `asHeld<T>()` does.

### Queries about the point set

- [`s.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aef424fd616b58f295831232bdbf8ee18 "Tests whether the wrapped shape covers no point at all."): Whether the point set covers no point. True for the [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane.") alternative and for any alternative in its own empty state, so a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") holding an empty [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") is [`empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aef424fd616b58f295831232bdbf8ee18 "Tests whether the wrapped shape covers no point at all.") without holding [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane.").
- [`s.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a9efef0c4a906867e35325d66642b6eec "Tests whether the point set is a single point."), [`s.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#affb1d4f593f794472e3e3e6210899edd "Tests whether the point set is a segment of positive length."), `s.getIfPoint<ResultNumber>()`, `s.getIfSegment<ResultNumber>()`: The collapsed point set, as the stored shape reports it ([degeneracies](shapes.md#degeneracies)). The `getIf…` pair returns an `std::optional`, and throws for a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") that collapses off the lattice of an integral `ResultNumber`.
- [`s.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0fae70d3db52396829bb71afb734d04e "Tests whether the wrapped shape is degenerate, as the held object defines it."), [`s.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a9273d2e6e907125e5251475ed0bc5788 "Tests whether the wrapped shape's defining data describes no shape, as the held object defines it."): The stored shape's own answers.
- [`s.dimension()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aca3a67938875e4871cbb270b2b532ac0 "Returns the dimension of the point set: -1 when empty, 0 for a point, 1 for a curve, 2 for a region."): `-1` for an empty point set, `0` for a point, `1` for a curve, `2` for a region — of the point set, so a triangle with collinear vertices is `1` and a collapsed one `0`.
- [`s.isBounded()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#af60a9008ed077ac88da73b8a31bbc849 "Tests whether the point set is bounded."): False for [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") and an unbounded [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."); true otherwise, the empty shape included.
- [`s.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0d8ddcea780ff8c6e77db983b6f2c9fd "Returns the wrapped shape's axis-aligned bounding box."): The bounding box, in the stored point type. Throws for the unbounded alternatives, for [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), and for an empty or unbounded [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.").
- `s.fbox<ResultNumber>()`: The floating-point box, over the same alternatives [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0d8ddcea780ff8c6e77db983b6f2c9fd "Returns the wrapped shape's axis-aligned bounding box.") covers. A [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") computes it from its center and radius, where [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0d8ddcea780ff8c6e77db983b6f2c9fd "Returns the wrapped shape's axis-aligned bounding box.") rounds that out to the stored point type.

### Queries about the defining data

These ask how the shape is written down rather than what it covers, so only the alternatives that store that kind of data answer and the rest throw.

- [`s.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a4dc27cef0528f6136d90f03f57604477 "isVertical of the wrapped shape."), [`s.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a6ea596783fd1af28bbaa75b6e244bb9d "isHorizontal of the wrapped shape."), `s.slope<ResultNumber>()`: For the linear alternatives — [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") and [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.").
- [`s.min()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac2870f7dfc6f54da74e332ebd9ce28db "The wrapped shape's min point."), [`s.max()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#abc8e5287b344fe5d8d6bfa3d3dd104aa "The wrapped shape's max point."): The lexicographic pair of defining points, for the linear alternatives and a [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.")'s two corners. Copies, not the references the concrete shapes return.
- [`s.source()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7770f18ef5ea9abc57b1034b20ebfde5 "The wrapped shape's source point."), [`s.target()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7b353f87a4bd2f6cc6802fe887a70377 "The wrapped shape's target point."): The ordered pair, for the alternatives that carry an orientation — [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") and [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.").
- [`s.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aa27e2e284ca41339e5724dc9da7e3cfa "isSimple of the wrapped shape."): Whether the ring or chain does not cross itself, for [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect."), [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.").

### Sequences

- `s.vertices<ResultNumber>()`, [`s.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a2e9544b04e51583b8e41cf2cfcae8598 "Returns the edges of the wrapped shape, as the held object's own edges()."), [`s.orientedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a9785a2641c75c69647eb8c39c2ce646f "Returns the oriented boundary edges of the wrapped shape, as the held object's own orientedEdges()."): The stored shape's sequences, as vectors. A [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") is its one vertex and a [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") its source; [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") and [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") have none. [`vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0a88ca44b45e8300c60895b44d8dfbb6 "Returns the vertices of the wrapped shape.") throws for a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), and for a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") vertex off the lattice of an integral `ResultNumber` — ask for a rational one, `vertices<pgl::ERational>()`. The edge sequences throw for every alternative with no edges: [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") and [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.").
- `s.latticePoints<ResultNumber>()`: The integer points the stored shape contains. Throws for [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") and the unbounded alternatives, and for an unbounded [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.").
- [`s.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0fa93c8ddd5f0c0f8e7fa1a874af942a "Returns the number of vertices of the wrapped shape."): The vertex count of the alternatives whose vertices span several rings or components, [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."). Every other alternative throws here and counts with [`vertices().size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0a88ca44b45e8300c60895b44d8dfbb6 "Returns the vertices of the wrapped shape.") — not with [`size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a292b0e51d6b29d8bf08f5fbf9781fa8b "Returns the number of indexable elements of the wrapped shape."), which counts defining points, two for a [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.") that has no vertex at all.
- [`s.size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a292b0e51d6b29d8bf08f5fbf9781fa8b "Returns the number of indexable elements of the wrapped shape."), [`s.get(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac46e9c696014dd135e14b17a433e4be4 "Returns the i-th vertex (modulo size()) of the wrapped shape."), `s[i]`, [`s.index(point)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ad250c2480f9e18c951448ebf5a955a9a "Returns the smallest index i with (*this)[i] == point, or -1 if no vertex of the wrapped shape equals point."): [Indexed access](shape_methods.md#indexed-access) to the stored shape's defining points. [`size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a292b0e51d6b29d8bf08f5fbf9781fa8b "Returns the number of indexable elements of the wrapped shape.") throws for [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."), whose vertices are spread over several rings or components. The point-valued accessors throw for those two, for [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), which has no element, and for the alternatives whose elements are not vertices: [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."), whose elements are coordinates, and [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), whose elements are half-planes. Reach through with `getIfHolds…` to use the concrete shape's own accessors.

### Measures and distances

- `s.area<ResultNumber>()`, `s.length<ResultNumber>()`, `s.centroid<ResultNumber>()`: Forwarded to the stored shape, and throwing for an alternative that has none. A [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") computes its area in floating point and converts.
- [`squaredDistance`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5a9d5d0a06f509e02f2f1ef4efe9763c "Returns the squared Euclidean distance to the given shape."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a40767b48c26b752e238898446828b2bf "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a87f914acfedb50b3972b23542c3fee54 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), [`squaredHausdorffDistance`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a99c878fe08c681555119d7ae3f1b0173 "Returns the squared Euclidean Hausdorff distance to the given shape."), [`hausdorffDistanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#afc9eb3f97fa0edd11f54779a09bbe33b "Returns the Manhattan (L1) Hausdorff distance to the given shape."), [`hausdorffDistanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a1c67b94b16694b02758b5874cee90ca6 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) Hausdorff distance to the given shape."): The [distances](shape_methods.md#other-methods-for-shapes) of the concrete pair, throwing for a pair with none. They default to `division_result_t<NumberType>` rather than to the pair-specific default, and a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") pair's floating answer is converted into it.
- `s.closestPoints<ResultNumber>(t)`, `s.closestSegments<ResultNumber>(t)`: The pair of points, or of elements, realizing the distance, and nothing when the shapes meet. A [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") accepts every pair and throws for one the concrete shapes do not define.
- `s.twiceArea<ResultNumber>()`, `s.diameter<ResultNumber>()`: Both default to `division_result_t<NumberType>` where the concrete shapes default to the native type, because a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") and a three-point [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") divide; ask for `twiceArea<NumberType>()` to get the concrete shapes' own type. [`twiceArea`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#abb570664bb6c51febed9077d6b5f088a "Returns twice the area of the wrapped shape.") throws for [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") and [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect."); [`diameter`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a9bd6d028fd3e6576494634d5b55b3121 "Returns a segment realizing the diameter of the wrapped shape.") throws for [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."), the unbounded alternatives and every [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.").
- `s.lengthL1<ResultNumber>()`, `s.lengthLInf<ResultNumber>()`, `s.squaredLength<ResultNumber>()`: The exact lengths, for [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") and [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), and the first two also for [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") and [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.").
- `s.pointInside<ResultNumber>()`, `s.midpoint<ResultNumber>()`, `s.center<ResultNumber>()`, `s.verticesCentroid<ResultNumber>()`: The stored shape's constructed points. [`pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aeb697b0c8f66b4f24dd05bed692b5c40 "The wrapped shape's pointInside.") answers for every alternative but [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane.") and [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."); [`midpoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a847007e7b9a7fbb814b3ae88b354606e "The wrapped shape's midpoint.") for [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label.") and [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."); [`center()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac7a469c719b74f2b6b1685de06b05109 "The wrapped shape's center.") for [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") and [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."); [`verticesCentroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a2a042fef84fce8b6a3df469e652d7ee4 "The wrapped shape's verticesCentroid.") for [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.").

### Predicates

[`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a1d453e908de41b5638c6a52f7571d64f "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a395b3a3a303fedc82f0ea4baeb7feb98 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aba0dd9903331c878d6e96ad45410c3b3 "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A ⊇ B)."), [`intersects`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a57b31eb2db4ca01e039b66d16b0c602c "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅)."), [`interiorsIntersect`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#af62d38c2b36469ea27a8758b77380bde "Tests whether the interiors of the two shapes intersect ((A∖∂A) ∩ (B∖∂B) ≠ ∅)."), [`separates`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#afaf680fe85dea507a43059c40aab6fd7 "Tests whether removing this shape disconnects the other shape (B∖A is disconnected)."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac6158ac2552661762f8792cdecfa51a1 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other).") and [`samePointSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#add5bda5f4fe1641cec5dae12b3f64e28 "Tests whether another shape defines exactly the same point set.") answer as the stored shape answers against the other operand ([predicates](shape_methods.md#predicates)). Every shape defines every predicate against every alternative, so these are the operations a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") never throws for.

The predicates about the defining data are defined for far fewer pairs, and throw for the rest.

- [`s.verticesContain(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ad4859ad72592f41c57d851a15848569f "Tests whether some defining point of this shape equals the given point."), [`s.containsEndpoint(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7c5086cf67f9b7a456c194f7e3b97f0a "Tests whether the given point is an endpoint of this shape."), [`s.containsCollinear(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a4b3404c239eab229b8620de7cf1d84d7 "Tests whether the given point, already known to be collinear with this shape, lies on it."), [`s.orientation(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5405a752a2b352dab1f1f34912d62eaa "Returns which side of this oriented shape the given point lies on."): Each needs a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") on the right, wrapped or concrete, and throws for anything else. [`verticesContain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ad4859ad72592f41c57d851a15848569f "Tests whether some defining point of this shape equals the given point.") answers for the linear alternatives, [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices.") and [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."); [`containsEndpoint`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7c5086cf67f9b7a456c194f7e3b97f0a "Tests whether the given point is an endpoint of this shape.") for [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") and [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."); [`containsCollinear`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a4b3404c239eab229b8620de7cf1d84d7 "Tests whether the given point, already known to be collinear with this shape, lies on it.") for those two and a [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."); [`orientation`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5405a752a2b352dab1f1f34912d62eaa "Returns which side of this oriented shape the given point lies on.") for [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") and [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.").
- [`s.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0fc388bd1bb664d72e3a003f174dc365 "Tests whether this shape and the other are parallel."), [`s.collinear(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a21fb5c42ada2b5e5adc9e139f96f0678 "Tests whether this shape and the other are collinear."): Both sides must be linear, except that [`collinear`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a21fb5c42ada2b5e5adc9e139f96f0678 "Tests whether this shape and the other are collinear.") also takes a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.").
- [`s.interiorContainsInterior(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a04f4034ad3e8f29011024b8cdc0ef231 "Tests whether the interior of this shape contains the interior of the other shape, which must be a segment."): A [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") or [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") against a segment.
- [`s.pointInsideInteriorContainedIn(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ad3bc6ffad51dcd6eb3e54b1d177d4962 "Tests whether this shape's pointInside() witness lies in the strict interior of the other shape."): Whether this shape's [`pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aeb697b0c8f66b4f24dd05bed692b5c40 "The wrapped shape's pointInside.") witness lies in the strict interior of `t`. Throws for the [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane."), [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") alternatives.

### Constructions

- `s.intersection<ResultNumber>(t)`: The connected pieces of the point-set intersection, as a `std::vector<Shape>` — empty for a disjoint pair, one element when the intersection is connected. Throws for a pair with no [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5d1599cde109c2e6d956ce7cc18b5700 "Returns the connected pieces of the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B)."), such as anything against a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.").
- `s.regularizedUnion<ResultNumber>(t)`, `s.difference<ResultNumber>(t)`, `s.regularizedIntersection<ResultNumber>(t)`, `s.symmetricDifference<ResultNumber>(t)`: The [boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations), returning a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") rather than a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes."), since every pair that has one answers with a set of regions. [`regularizedUnion`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aeef3526dcbf2086536735d10912dac3b "Returns the regularized union closure(A° ∪ B°).") and [`symmetricDifference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a50c250b96b51b8930f038b501a8a1cc7 "Returns the regularized symmetric difference of the two shapes (A △ B).") need both alternatives to be a bounded polygonal region — [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") or [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."). [`difference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a1a9969abd20d8df944bb9db439dd7812 "Returns the regularized set difference of the two shapes (A ∖ B).") needs that on the left and admits a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") or [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") as the subtrahend. [`regularizedIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a4e804cfa43413b4bdfc610647503f6af "Returns the regularized intersection closure(A° ∩ B°) of two region-valued shapes.") needs a [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") or [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") on one side.
- [`s.minkowskiSum(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a085ead80751f84a3a8ab96078ced77b3 "Returns the Minkowski sum of this shape and another (A ⊕ B)."), [`s.minkowskiErosion(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac8361380d687fb83b767e753d6080ccf "Returns the Minkowski erosion of this shape by another (A ⊖ B)."): The [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum) and [erosion](shape_methods.md#minkowski-erosion), re-wrapped in a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes."). Both compile for every operand and throw when the stored pair has no such answer, or when it has one the wrapper's point type cannot hold — an erosion that is a rational [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") does not fit a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") over integer points.
- `s.convexHull<ResultNumber>()`: Throws for the empty shape, the unbounded alternatives and a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), and for a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") that is empty, unbounded, or has a vertex off the lattice of an integral `ResultNumber`.
- [`s.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aaf07e7ce121d43de1608b37bc9cb335b "Returns the wrapped region as a PolygonWithHoles."): The stored shape as a region, for the alternatives that have such a conversion.
- [`s.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac51f9a1170f55b0fcdd962167e29273f "The wrapped shape as a Line."), [`s.asOrientedLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a2be526f15ce58c95907a4661624a4f02 "The wrapped shape as a OrientedLine."), [`s.asPolyline()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a52939209909b6366dadf0b5d2a14aa51 "The wrapped shape as a Polyline."), [`s.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5fb89146d962ed639473babcd7fba436 "The wrapped shape as a Polygon."), [`s.asPolygonSet()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a134c9229e5fdf256791c92ba649998c8 "The wrapped shape as a PolygonSet."), [`s.asHalfplaneIntersection()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0afbc5f42b5247b5a54be1932180ed9d "The wrapped shape as a HalfplaneIntersection."), `s.asConvex<ResultNumber>()`: The stored shape's own conversions, each throwing for an alternative that has none. An alternative that is already the target type comes back as it is. [`asConvex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#af5dc9b1e738a92a6f7dc0694a790c858 "Returns the wrapped shape as a Convex.") takes a `ResultNumber` because a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.")'s vertices are implicit.
- [`s.halfplaneAbove()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a0c6ac078fb67d406cfff920c98676b1d "The wrapped shape's halfplaneAbove."), [`s.halfplaneBelow()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#afaf7cd1ab42527a26160c2c7727ea66a "The wrapped shape's halfplaneBelow."), [`s.leftHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a93cc275442d196abce0884e721cf0ca8 "The wrapped shape's leftHalfplane."), [`s.rightHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a02cc590221a2bb904f5b237a1031b49f "The wrapped shape's rightHalfplane."): The half-planes a linear shape bounds — the first pair for [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") and [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), the second for [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") and [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.").
- [`s.opposite()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a746a6b194a03ba4424f63fb4920004ad "Returns the wrapped shape with its orientation reversed."): The stored shape with its orientation reversed, as a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") holding the same alternative. For [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") and [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.").
- [`s.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a300721886c0b5c36c10c3f0f53671d28 "Returns the circumscribed disk of the wrapped shape."): The circumscribed [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") of a [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") or a [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices.").
- `s.dual<ResultNumber>()`, `s.polar<ResultNumber>()`: The [dual and polar](shape_methods.md#other-methods-for-shapes) images, as a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") — a line for a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") and a point for a [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), so which alternative comes back is known only at run time. Both default to `division_result_t<NumberType>` for that reason: the [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.") direction divides.
- [`s.convexPartition()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aa5e44f09026f5b1eddd18f0f8058a5ac "Cuts the wrapped region into Convex pieces with disjoint interiors."), [`s.convexCovering()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7bfcd74b5ffccef6801161ac49e8e436 "Returns an irredundant covering of the wrapped region by Convex pieces, which may overlap."), [`s.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ab5de8d11bbd09248ed0eb44a56aaa3d4 "Returns the constrained Delaunay triangulation of the wrapped region."), `s.asBitMatrix<ResultNumber>()`: The region decompositions, for [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."). [`asBitMatrix`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aaf500d0aaf1b8afbf1683db5e4388d03 "Returns the wrapped rectilinear region rasterized into a BitMatrix.") still requires a rectilinear region.

### Mixing wrapped and concrete operands

Every binary operation takes a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") or a concrete shape on either side, so the two styles mix freely.

```C++
pgl::Shape r = pgl::Rectangle(1,4,2,9);
r.intersects(pgl::Segment(0,0,5,5));   // concrete argument
pgl::Segment(0,0,5,5).intersection(r); // concrete receiver, wrapped argument: a std::vector<Shape>
```

The answer comes back in the wrapper's shape, not the receiver's: [`segment.intersection(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5d1599cde109c2e6d956ce7cc18b5700 "Returns the connected pieces of the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") is a vector of [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes."), where [`segment.intersection(otherSegment)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a5d1599cde109c2e6d956ce7cc18b5700 "Returns the connected pieces of the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") is the tight `std::optional<std::variant<Point, Segment>>`, because which alternative the argument holds is not known until run time.

A concrete receiver takes a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") for a construction or a distance only when it has that operation against some alternative, so a call no stored alternative could answer stays a compile error instead of a call certain to throw: [`segment.regularizedUnion(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#aeef3526dcbf2086536735d10912dac3b "Returns the regularized union closure(A° ∪ B°).") does not compile, while `Shape(segment).regularizedUnion(shape)` compiles and throws. The predicates need no such gate.

### Transformations

- `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, [`rotate90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#afe8cef409e221c8370955e26c1438b7a "Rotates the wrapped shape by 90k degrees around the origin in place.") and the in-place axis scalings act on the stored shape and preserve both the alternative and the coordinate type; [`rotated90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#a7a054e7ce1b36d1e75c569bb528882af "Returns the wrapped shape rotated by 90k degrees around the origin.") and the `scaled…` methods return a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") of the same type. The free `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` promote the point type the way the concrete shapes do.
- The axis scalings ([`scaledUpX`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac2f25ba5c15576b11cf4200eff891720 "Returns the wrapped shape with its x-coordinates scaled up."), [`scaleUpX`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#ac2ac45dbd3ae776800f53dd5d31faab9 "Scales the wrapped shape's x-coordinates up in place.") and their siblings) throw for a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."), whose result would be an ellipse.
- `transformation * s` applies an [affine map](shape_methods.md#transformations) to the stored shape, and throws for the [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") and [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") alternatives, which cannot represent a parallelogram or an ellipse.

### Comparison, hashing and output

- `==` compares the stored alternative and value, so a [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") and a [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.") with the same point set differ; [`samePointSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html#add5bda5f4fe1641cec5dae12b3f64e28 "Tests whether another shape defines exactly the same point set.") compares point sets instead. `<=>` orders by alternative first, then by value.
- `std::hash` is specialized, so a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") goes directly into a `std::unordered_set` or `std::unordered_map`, and the ordering puts it into a `std::set`.
- `operator<<` streams the stored alternative, and a [`Canvas`](canvas.md) draws it. An [`Arrangement`](data_structures.md#arrangement) accepts a container of [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") as input.
